summary: Submitted a probe that targets the verify question's open gap by separating two things the earlier stall attempt conflated: a VerifyLeader request needs the leader's main loop to be registered, but the acknowledgement it counts arrives on replication goroutines, which a blocked main loop does not stop. Each trial registers the request while the leader is isolated from every peer, stalls its main loop inside StoreLogs for 900ms, then reconnects only the non-voter after 250-500ms — after a voter majority has had time to elect a successor — and reports the verify endpoint, when another server was first sampled in Leader state, whether that preceded the verdict, the terms and the stall counters. A construction run showed exactly that overlap: in all six trials another server led at term 3 from 372-518ms, before the verdict at about 931ms, and in four of them the isolated leader still returned verify success while remaining at term 2, so the same node was serving a stale-read verdict while its successor led. Three comparisons separate the success, the overlap and the conditional witness; execution is requested and no observation is claimed until the clean-copy receipt exists. Unfinished: interpreting that receipt and, if it holds, revising the parent question's gap from unresolved to answered and restating its consequence.
